function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity wasn’t “discovered” by one person at a single moment; it was uncovered gradually over centuries through the work of many scientists and thinkers. Here are some of the most influential contributors:

| Time | Key figure | Contribution |
|------|------------|--------------|
| **6th century BCE** | **Thales of Miletus** | First recorded observation of static electricity by rubbing amber. |
| **16th century** | **William Gilbert** | Published *De Magnete* (1600), distinguishing magnetism from static electricity and coining the term “electricity.” |
| **17th century** | **Otto von Guericke** | Demonstrated static electricity with the Leyden jar (1660). |
| **18th century** | **Benjamin Franklin** | Conducted kite‑experiment (1752), showing lightning is electrical; introduced positive/negative charge concepts. |
| **18th century** | **Alessandro Volta** | Invented the voltaic pile (1800), the first chemical battery, providing a steady electric current. |
| **19th century** | **Michael Faraday** | Discovered electromagnetic induction (1831) and formulated Faraday’s laws of induction. |
| **19th century** | **James Clerk Maxwell** | Unified electricity and magnetism into Maxwell’s equations (1860s). |

So, while no single individual “discovered” electricity, the cumulative work of these pioneers—and many others—led to our modern understanding of electric phenomena.
